en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape, which is easily visible from Legazpi City.
During the dry season, the grass covering the Chocolate Hills in Bohol dries up and turns a distinct chocolate brown.
The giant Rafflesia flower found in Mount Apo emits a strong smell of rotting meat to attract pollinating flies.
The main crater lake of Taal Volcano in Batangas occasionally changes its water color due to underwater geothermal activity.
The Amihan wind brings cool, dry air to the Philippines from November to February, resulting in clear, sunny skies.
The Philippine tarsier in Bohol has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain to help it see at night.
Mount Pulag in Benguet is famous for its sea of clouds, where hikers can literally stand above the cloud tops.
The stilt roots of coastal mangrove trees in Palawan trap sediments and provide a visible underwater nursery for young fish.
The sand at Pink Beach in Zamboanga gets its distinct rosy color from tiny fragments of crushed red coral.
The Philippine eagle, found in Mindanao forests, features a distinctive crest of long, shaggy brown feathers on its head.
The limestone ceilings of Callao Cave in Peñablanca feature visible, naturally formed stalactites created by dripping mineral water over centuries.
The surface of Lake Sebu in South Cotabato often acts like a mirror, clearly reflecting the surrounding green mountains during calm mornings.
